findings.title: Residual of closed #259: `import hypertools` still mutates matplotlib rcParams (backend_fallback True -> False)
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import copy, matplotlib
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
before = copy.deepcopy(dict(matplotlib.rcParams))
import hypertools
after = dict(matplotlib.rcParams)
print({k: (before[k], after[k]) for k in before if repr(before[k]) != repr(after[k])})"

findings.title: hyp.load() on an unsupported binary file (e.g. .png) raises a raw _pickle.UnpicklingError from dill internals instead of a clear 'unsupported file type' error
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
arr = np.zeros((8, 8, 3)); arr[::2, ::2] = [1, 0, 0]
plt.imsave('/tmp/tiny_x8.png', arr)
hyp.load('/tmp/tiny_x8.png')"
findings.expected: HypertoolsIOError: unsupported file type '.png' -- hyp.load() reads .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls and pickled .geo/.pkl (or similar)
findings.actual:
File ".../dill/_dill.py", line 453, in load
    obj = StockUnpickler.load(self)
_pickle.UnpicklingError: A load persistent id instruction was encountered, but no persistent_load function was specified.

findings.title: Hosted *_model example datasets are sklearn-1.0.2-era pickles: loading under the 1.0 stack (sklearn 1.8.0) emits InconsistentVersionWarning ('might lead to breaking code or invalid results')
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; m = hyp.load('wiki_model'); print(type(m).__name__)"
findings.expected: Model loads with no version-compatibility warnings (pickle created under the supported sklearn range), or documentation stating the warning is expected and outputs verified
findings.actual: sklearn/base.py:463: InconsistentVersionWarning: Trying to unpickle estimator LatentDirichletAllocation from version 1.0.2 when using version 1.8.0. This might lead to breaking code or invalid results. ... (repeated for CountVectorizer, Pipeline) then: Pipeline

findings.title: Model-spec kwarg naming is inconsistent across sibling dispatchers: hyp.align/hyp.manip use model=, hyp.cluster/hyp.reduce/hyp.normalize use the function's own name; first arg is x vs data
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
x = np.random.randn(30, 4)
hyp.cluster(x, model={'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 2}})"
findings.expected: Either accepted (model= alias) or an error suggesting the cluster= kwarg
findings.actual: TypeError: cluster() got an unexpected keyword argument 'model'

findings.title: hyp.plot figures are pyplot-unmanaged yet every figure carries fig.number == 1
findings.repro:
MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "
import numpy as np, matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
figs = [hyp.plot(np.random.randn(20, 3), '.', show=False) for _ in range(3)]
print(plt.get_fignums(), [f.number for f in figs], [f is plt.figure(1) for f in figs])"
findings.expected: Consistent state: either managed figures with unique numbers, or no misleading .number attribute
